Let
\[
C:=xy-h-h^2\in R.
\]
I claim
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k\bigl[C,h^5,x^5,y^5\bigr]\subset R.}
\]

First check that \(C\) is central. Since
\[
yx-xy=(\zeta^{-1}-1)h+(\zeta^{-2}-1)h^2,
\]
we have
\[
yx=C+\zeta^{-1}h+\zeta^{-2}h^2,\qquad xy=C+h+h^2.
\]
Using \(xh=\zeta hx\), one gets
\[
[x y,x]=x(yx-xy)=\bigl((1-\zeta)h+(1-\zeta^2)h^2\bigr)x,
\]
while
\[
[-h-h^2,x]=\bigl((\zeta-1)h+(\zeta^2-1)h^2\bigr)x,
\]
so \([C,x]=0\). Similarly, using \(yh=\zeta^{-1}hy\), one gets \([C,y]=0\), and clearly \([C,h]=0\). Thus \(C\in Z(R)\).

Now write \(A=k[h,C]\). Then \(R\) is the generalized Weyl algebra over \(A\) with automorphism
\[
\sigma(h)=\zeta h,\qquad \sigma(C)=C,
\]
and relation
\[
xy=C+h+h^2.
\]
Because \(\sigma^5=\mathrm{id}\), the elements \(h^5,x^5,y^5\) commute with \(h,C,x,y\), hence
\[
k[C,h^5,x^5,y^5]\subseteq Z(R).
\]

Conversely, \(R\) has the usual \(\mathbb Z\)-grading
\[
R=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb Z} R_n,\qquad R_n=A x^n\ (n>0),\quad R_0=A,\quad R_{-n}=A y^n.
\]
If a homogeneous element of degree \(n\) is central, then commuting with \(h\) forces
\[
\zeta^n=1,
\]
so \(5\mid n\). Thus only degrees divisible by \(5\) can occur in a central element.

For degree \(0\), centrality means an element \(a(h,C)\in A\) must satisfy
\[
\sigma(a)=a,
\]
so
\[
a\in A^\sigma=k[C,h^5].
\]
For degree \(5m\), the homogeneous part is an element of \(A x^{5m}\) or \(A y^{5m}\). Since \(x^5,y^5\) are already central, centrality again forces the coefficient to lie in \(A^\sigma=k[C,h^5]\). Hence every central element lies in
\[
k[C,h^5,x^5,y^5].
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k\bigl[xy-h-h^2,\ h^5,\ x^5,\ y^5\bigr].}
\]

Equivalently, if \(C=xy-h-h^2\) and \(H=h^5\), then the generators satisfy
\[
x^5y^5
=\prod_{i=0}^4\bigl(C+\zeta^i h+\zeta^{2i}h^2\bigr)
=H^2+(1-5C+5C^2)H+C^5.
\]
